quiz.question: What distinguishes a Raspberry Pi from a typical microcontroller?

answers.answer: It can only run one program at a time in a loop
It runs a full Linux operating system with a desktop environment
It has no USB or HDMI ports
It requires a separate Wi-Fi adapter to connect to the internet

quiz.explanation: A Raspberry Pi is a full Linux computer the size of a credit card, with USB ports, HDMI output, Wi-Fi, and a desktop OS, unlike a basic microcontroller that runs a single program without an operating system.

quiz.question: What feature allows a Raspberry Pi to interact with physical hardware like LEDs and sensors?
quiz.explanation: The GPIO (General Purpose Input/Output) pins along one edge of the Pi let your code talk directly to LEDs, sensors, and motors, while you still have the full OS for debugging and networking.

quiz.question: Why is having a full operating system useful when doing hardware projects on a Raspberry Pi?

answers.answer: It makes the Pi cheaper to manufacture
It provides debugging, networking, and file management alongside hardware control
It eliminates the need for GPIO pins
It ensures the board has no boot time

quiz.explanation: A full OS gives you access to debugging tools, networking capabilities, and file management, all of which are helpful when building and troubleshooting hardware projects.
